title: CSV reader
skill: Say what happens with short and long rows

good: Rewrite parse_csv(text) in csv_reader.py. The first row is the header; each later row becomes a dict of header name -> field. Fields are split by commas. A field in double quotes can hold commas, newlines and doubled quotes ("" means one "). Rows end with \n or \r\n. A newline at the very end adds no row; empty text returns []. A row with fewer fields than the header gets "" for the missing ones. A row with more fields than the header raises ValueError. csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline="")) is fine, but not DictReader's defaults. Only change csv_reader.py. Then run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
lazy: Make parse_csv handle real CSV files.
